samples.claim: Flat takes fixed-width data to one buffer, with positive bits_per_value uint64=1 (not necessarily byte multiple) and optional BufferCompression data=2. Variable takes variable-width data to compressed offsets CompressiveEncoding=1 plus a value buffer with optional BufferCompression values=2. The prose calls them transparent/uncompressed leaves, but their declared optional buffer compression invokes the opacity rule above; readers must interpret those comments conditionally rather than ignore data/values compression (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:385-407).

411 |  *
412 |  * This is a leaf encoding, there is no compression applied to the data.
413 |  *
414 |  * This is a transparent encoding by definition.
415 |  *
416 |  * The input is a fixed-width data block.
417 |  * The output is a single buffer.
418 |  */

420 |   /* the number of bits per value, must be greater than 0, does

samples.claim: Initialize prev_row to 0..=n and curr_row to n+1 zeros. For each s1 char set first current cost i+1; each s2 char has substitution cost0 when equal else1; current[j+1] is min(previous[j+1]+1,current[j]+1,previous[j]+cost), then swap row buffers. Return prev_row[n]. Time is O(m*n) after O(m+n) character collection; two DP rows use O(n), but total auxiliary storage includes both character vectors and is O(m+n). Row width follows s2, not min(m,n). No early cutoff, Result, unsafe code, shared state or IO exists; allocation/arithmetic failures are not caught.
samples.review_note: Matches recurrence and two-row storage; sample14 confirms both Unicode character vectors.

samples.claim: pub fn levenshtein_distance(s1:&str,s2:&str)->usize collects both strings into Vec<char>, counts m/n and returns the other length if either is empty. Both character vectors are constructed before empty checks; empty collection need not allocate heap storage. Comparison is exact, case-sensitive, without normalization or grapheme segmentation. Non-ASCII scalar values count as one element regardless of UTF-8 byte width. Character equality and recurrence are at rust/lance-core/src/levenshtein.rs:34-40.
samples.review_note: Matches char vectors and early empty returns; sample8 confirms exact equality recurrence.

samples.claim: build_predicate receives slice::Iter<u64>. Bitmap/Set compute !contains(id as u32) for every address into Vec<bool>, then convert to BooleanArray: true means retain/not deleted, false deleted, and values are non-null. Casting discards the high fragment half, so callers must apply the single-fragment deletion vector to the correct fragment. NoDeletions returns None, but an empty Set/Bitmap returns Some(all true), including Some(empty) on empty input. This is not a fragment-ID validator or a stable-row-ID remapper.
samples.evidence:

105 |     // Note: deletion vectors are based on 32-bit offsets.  However, this function works
106 |     // even when given 64-bit row addresses.  That is because `id as u32` returns the lower
107 |     // 32 bits (the row offset) and the upper 32 bits are ignored.
108 |     pub fn build_predicate(&self, row_addrs: std::slice::Iter<u64>) -> Option<BooleanArray> {
109 |         match self {
110 |             Self::Bitmap(bitmap) => Some(
111 |                 row_addrs
112 |                     .map(|&id| !bitmap.contains(id as u32))
113 |                     .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
114 |             ),

118 |                     .collect::<Vec<_>>(),

122 |         .map(BooleanArray::from)

124 | }
